_comment: Live transcription of the HUMAN leg of the call - the part OpenAI Realtime does not give us
for free, because on that leg nothing is listening. Each browser transcribes its OWN
microphone and posts the finished lines; no audio is stored, by either side, exactly as on the
AI leg.
Everything here is read at request time, so the protocol can be corrected without a rebuild.
That matters more than usual: this was written to the documentation rather than against a
live endpoint, and the first real proof is a pilot call.
Do NOT add turn_detection here. The service refuses it outright - "Turn detection is not
supported for this transcription model", invalid_value on session.audio.input.turn_detection -
and the refusal is of the whole session, so transcription simply does not happen. This model
segments speech itself; the assistant's session.json takes VAD settings and this one does not.
client.socketPath: {model} is replaced with the deployment name. If the socket will not open
(a TRANSCRIBE_ERROR at stage 'socket'), this is the thing to vary - the close code in the
detail says how it failed. Known candidates, in order of likelihood:
/realtime?model={model}        - the token already carries the transcription session
/realtime?intent=transcription - OpenAI's own documented form; reported to redirect on Azure
/realtime                      - everything carried by the ephemeral key
model: the Azure DEPLOYMENT name, which is whatever it was called when deployed - not
necessarily the model name. Empty disables transcription entirely and the call runs as before.
participantSide: both sides are transcribed. The ethics approval permits transcription and
forbids RECORDING, which is the distinction this implements: the samples go to the recogniser
and the finished text comes back, and no audio is written down anywhere by either side. Set it
to false to transcribe only the agent.
